officialSummary: It may be recalled that in February 2004 , the Reserve Bank initiated the practice of compiling half-yearly reports on the management of foreign exchange reserves and making them public to promote greater transparency and enhance disclosure in the management of the country’s foreign exchange reserves. In this connection, Reserve Bank of India has today released the 47th Half-Yearly Report on Management of Foreign Exchange Reserves with reference to end-September 2026. During April-September 2026, India’s foreign exchange reserves increased from US$ 691.11 billion to US$ 737.78 billion. The latest position of India’s foreign exchange reserves is available at the following link: https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/WSSView.aspx?Id=28849 (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1564
title: 47th Half-Yearly Report on Management of Foreign Exchange Reserves: April – September 2026

officialSummary: Today, the Reserve Bank released the November 2026 issue of its monthly Bulletin. The Bulletin includes six speeches, four articles and current statistics. The four articles are: I. State of the Economy; II. Shifting Drivers of Imported Inflation: COVID-19 Pandemic to the West Asia Conflict; III. Performance of the NBFC Sector during 2025-26: A Review; and IV. Disentangling the Impact of US Monetary Policy on Indian Financial Markets: An Event Study Approach. I. State of the Economy Supply side challenges, elevated energy prices, and geopolitical uncertainty remain significant headwinds to the global economic outlook. Persistent inflationary pressures have led to synchronised monetary policy tightening across major central banks in the last three months. Pullback in AI-related stocks and elevated sovereign bond yields, despite some softening from multi-decade highs, remain a source of volatility in financial markets. Amidst uneven economic performance globally, the Indian economy stood out. High-frequency indicators of domestic economic activity showed resilience in October, underpinned by strong credit demand. Headline CPI inflation inched up, primarily driven by higher food inflation. With strong exports performance, the trade deficit narrowed in October as compared to corresponding month of the previous year. Equity markets rebounded supported by robust corporate earnings and foreign portfolio inflows. Net inflows under ECB and NRI deposits also remained strong. II. Shifting Drivers of Imported Inflation: COVID-19 Pandemic to the West Asia Conflict By Snehal S. Herwadkar, Ishu Thakur, Abhiruchi Rathi, Paras and Parul Arora This article examines how successive global shocks have reshaped the drivers of imported inflation in India.
